To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we developed an IE system that extracts regulatory interactions for E.coli; (ii) we designed an ontology that contains knowledge about E.coli and its regulatory networks, (iii) we generalized the IE system to use the knowledge in the ontology; and (iv) we tested the IE system with abstracts and full articles and obtained good results.

we developed a system that can extract regulatory networks from scientific papers using an ontology, and we tested this system with abstract and full papers that describe regulatory interactions of Escherichia Coli, and the results are satisfactory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of IE systems that can be applied to different domains.
the automatic extraction of regulatory interactions between genes and transcription factors, which are represented as a graph.
the development and testing of an IE system that identifies the regulatory networks of E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ontology-based IE system is able to extract regulatory interactions with a precision of 90% and a recall of 70%.
the proposed system is a first step in the generalization of the existing IE method for E. coli to other domains.

, although there are some problems that need further work (e.g., the lack of a general method for detecting the gene name), the system is able to correctly identify a significant number of the regulatory networks described in the scientific literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by applying the proposed methodology, we obtained an IE system that is able to automatically extract regulatory networks from abstracts of scientific papers.
we have designed and populated a domain ontology for the Molecular Biology domain and we have generalized an existing IE system to work with it.
we have developed an ontology-based IE system for regulatory network extraction from scientific articles, which can be used for any domain that has a database of the same kind as RegulonDB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a domain ontology can be used as a basis to generalize an IE system, which is an important step in the direction of the development of general-purpose IE systems for the Molecular Biology domain.
a generalization of an existing IE system to a different domain is not a trivial task, but it can be achieved with a reasonable amount of effort.
a system based on a general ontology can be used for extracting regulatory networks from scientific papers in different organisms.
